messages:
tariq: seeing a spike in apiserver 500s and a ton of watch reconnects in ap-southeast1 starting ~03:10 UTC. GPU attach failures jumped at the same time. controller-manager queue growing.
maya: yep, alerted me. looks like large fanout to apiserver + NAT saturation. dash: https://dash.internal/redwood/region/ap-southeast1/overview
alex: grabbing node conntrack stats now. suspect CNAT port exhaustion and lots of concurrent attach RPCs from provisioner. previously we saw similar when attach churn hit high qps.
sre-oncall-bot: INCIDENT_OPENED: apiserver_5xx_surge_ap-southeast1 Alert: 5xx_rate > 2% for 10m. Incident page: https://incidents/redwood/INC-20260320-99
jo: logs from apiserver-0: several TLS handshake timeouts and websocket closes while handling watches:
```
E030 03:12:35.789 apiserver.go:412] watch: websocket close 1006 unexpected EOF
E030 03:12:36.001 apiserver.go:498] http2: server response header connection error: net/http: TLS handshake timeout
```
tariq: conntrack count on node-7: 65528/65536. lots of CLOSE_WAIT sockets.
maya: don't want to reboot controlplane unless absolutely needed. can we limit provisioner concurrency quickly? lower blast radius first.
alex: mitigation options (fast -> slow):
- set provisioner ATTACH_CONCURRENCY=6 in region canary
- increase provisioner backoff from 200ms -> 1s
- temporarily provision an extra NAT gateway for ap-southeast1
- bump net.netfilter.nf_conntrack_max across nodes and roll a small batch
ops-bot: cost note: extra NAT gateway ~ $1.4k/mo. kernel conntrack bump is infra config change (low $) but requires image bake & rollout.
tariq: applying canary throttle to provisioner in ap-southeast1 now.
alex: command (running):
```
kubectl -n infra set env deploy/provisioner ATTACH_CONCURRENCY=6 ATTACH_BACKOFF_MS=1000
```
jo: also add a simple rate limiter at provisioner front to flatten attach bursts. even a leaky-bucket of 50 r/s helps.
maya: if that reduces apiserver fanout and 5xxs drop, keep throttled for 24h while we schedule a proper fix. I'll draft RFC for long-term: attach batching, circuit breaker, NAT autoscale policy.
sre-oncall-bot: NOTE: 5xx rate climbed to 3.4% at 03:18 UTC  escalation threshold met.
alex: canary applied. metrics: apiserver watch reconnects down ~30% in 90s, provisioner attach error rate down 45%.
tariq: great. keeping watch on etcd leader latency & controller-manager retries. if we see leader election churn, immediate rollback.
ops-bot: also consider short-term kernel param tweak on a small node pool: sysctl net.netfilter.nf_conntrack_max=262144 then promote if stable. risk: more sockets, need to ensure memory headroom.
jo: when stable, we'll run a staged stress test in staging to try to reproduce the conntrack leak path with simultaneous NVMe compaction + attach churn.
maya: opened a tracking RFC: https://rfc.internal/redwood/attach-scaling-2026, will include harvest of postmortems and proposed NAT autoscaler rules.
alex: I'll follow up with a small PR to make ATTACH_CONCURRENCY a config flag and add region overrides. planning eu-west1 canary tomorrow.
sre-oncall-bot: INCIDENT_UPDATE: mitigation applied (provisioner throttle); monitoring for 5xx < 1% over 1h to auto-close.
tariq: thanks team. leaving throttled for now; will update if leader election or etcd P99 write latency worsens.
maya: thumbs up. :thumbsup:
